task.name: A high preflight complexity score buys accommodation but never prompts a scope decision, so an over-broad story is planned at full cost
task.story_text:
---
depends_on:
  - issue-2680
---

## Problem

Preflight scores a story's complexity for roughly $0.37 and forge then spends the
remaining 98% of the run not acting on that number. A high score buys longer timeouts
and stronger models; it never prompts a question. Issue #2541 scored 9, ran twice for
$43.64, and never reached DEV. It turned out to contain four independently deliverable
pieces of work, which landed for $86.11 once split — a judgment the operator made by
hand, after the money was spent, from evidence forge already had before planning began.

Cost is concentrated after the score is known. On the second #2541 run, preflight was
$0.37, planning $3.77, and plan review $29.25. Every dollar past preflight was spent on
a story the score had already flagged.

Human teams handle this with a soft ceiling: past some estimate, someone asks whether
the work should be split before it is planned in detail. The number is a rough up-front
judgment, not the product of deep analysis, and it triggers a conversation rather than
a refusal. Forge computes the equivalent number and discards its only cheap opportunity
to use it.

Forge has two existing scope refusals and neither has ever protected a run: the intake
cluster heuristic admitted #2541, and the planner's decompose signal has not fired in
any recorded run. A gate that ships inactive would be a third. This one is active by
default, with the threshold configurable in both directions.

Depends on #2680: the shipped default threshold must be chosen against the range of
scores that are actually reachable.

## What

At a configurable preflight complexity threshold, active by default, a run pauses
before it spends anything further and asks the operator to approve the story as scoped
or return it for decomposition.

## Acceptance criteria

- A story whose preflight verdict is PROCEED and whose complexity score reaches the
  configured threshold blocks before any cost-bearing phase that follows preflight, and
  reports the score and the decision awaiting the operator. The gate is anchored to the
  end of preflight, not to any one downstream phase, so a story that skips planning
  because preflight classified it implementation-ready still stops here.
- A story whose preflight verdict is not PROCEED never blocks on this gate.
- The threshold is configurable and ships active with a default value. Raising the
  threshold above the highest score preflight can assign disables the gate; no separate
  enable switch exists, and a run with the shipped configuration emits the pause.
- An operator decision to approve logs the story as explicitly approved at that score,
  and the run continues exactly as it would have without the gate.
- An operator decision to decompose exits the run without spending on any later phase,
  and reports the story as returned for decomposition rather than as a story that
  failed.
- Other stories in the same sprint continue while one story waits. A story awaiting this
  decision never blocks a story that does not depend on it.
- When no decision arrives within the configured wait, the run takes the configured
  no-decision action, which accepts only the same two values an operator may choose, and
  reports which action it took and that no operator decision was recorded. The shipped
  no-decision action returns the story for decomposition. Configuration that is absent,
  empty, or not one of the two accepted values also returns the story rather than
  proceeding, so no misconfiguration can spend on an unapproved story.

## Example

A sprint reaches the gate on a story scoring at the threshold. The decision is keyed by
the story's own run id, as reported by `forge status`, not by the sprint's:

```
▸ #2541  PREFLIGHT  complexity 9 (impl 9, validation 3)  — awaiting operator
  Threshold 9 (default). Nothing has been spent beyond preflight for this story.

    forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af approve      plan and implement it as scoped
    forge decide 7c1e04b9d3af decompose    return it to be split

  No decision within 30m: decompose (default). Other stories continue meanwhile.
```

Approving proceeds unchanged and records the approval, so a large-but-cohesive story is
never blocked by its size alone. Returning it costs the $0.37 already spent on preflight
instead of the $43.64 that #2541 actually cost.

conventions_soft[0].value: Coordinator is pure Python — no LLM calls for routing or process decisions

conventions_soft[1].value: Schema validation is the integrity boundary — do not relax cross-validation rules

conventions_soft[2].value: Keep modules single-purpose. Extract when a responsibility separates from its neighbours — never to satisfy a line count. Putting a change in an already-large module is correct if that is where it belongs; a module carved at whatever line got the count down is worse than the large module it came from.

conventions_soft[3].value: Keep pure-data types in low-dependency modules with stdlib-only imports

conventions_soft[4].value: Separate prompt construction, output parsing, and coordinator control flow

conventions_soft[5].value: When adding or modifying data that flows between coordinator phases, instrument the change so the actual values are visible in the audit trail — diagnosing sprint failures requires tracing real data, not reconstructing it

conventions_soft[6].value: Do not create files outside src/, tests/, or docs/. If you need a scratch file for exploration, delete it before committing.

conventions_soft[7].value: Changes that affect coordinator phase boundaries, state handoff between phases, or adaptive routing/config propagation must include seam-level integration tests covering the touched boundary. Unit tests alone are insufficient when correctness depends on cross-phase state flow.

preflight.reason: This adds a new pending-decision gate at the end of preflight, closely modeled on the existing PLAN_REVIEW/ESCALATE/HUMAN_REVIEW pending-file HITL gates (pending_hitl.py, pending.py, and the already-generic `forge decide` CLI command), plus a new config section analogous to PlanReviewConfig. It is a single coherent seam reusing well-established infra rather than several independently landable pieces, but it is coordinator phase-boundary surgery, which this project's own scoring rules treat as large regardless of edit count.

plan_review.findings:
- [P1-impl] [openai-gpt-5.6-sol-cli] Steps 1 and 5 necessarily change the canonical audit-record shape: RetryPolicy fields are automatically flattened under configuration.recorded_values, and Step 5 adds a distinct gate audit block/outcome. tests/test_audit_schema_guard.py::test_audit_record_schema_unchanged requires every such shape change to bump CURRENT_RECORD_SCHEMA_VERSION, add the corresponding MIGRATION_HELPERS entry, and commit a new schema snapshot. The plan lists coordinator/audit.py but omits src/theforge/coordinator/audit_storage.py and tests/fixtures/audit_record_schema_v39.json, so the authoritative gate will predictably fail and historical records will lack the required migration.
  Suggestion: Extend Step 5/7 to bump the audit record version in audit_storage.py, add the v38-to-v39 migration and registry entry, regenerate and commit audit_record_schema_v39.json, and run test_audit_schema_guard.py.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Carried risk 2 (decompose does not fit the success/failure binary). Step 5 lists story_state.py/runner.py/status_reader.py/audit.py, but StoryOutcome has ~126 call sites across sprint/state_writer.py, sprint/rca.py, sprint/abnormal.py, sprint/budget_runtime.py and cli/sprint.py that Step 5 does not name. A new enum member that is omitted from _TERMINAL_OUTCOMES (story_state.py:124) or _CANONICAL_TO_LEGACY_STATUS (story_state.py:149) would leave the story non-terminal — the sprint could re-dispatch or hang on it — and the runner's if not result.success paths (runner.py:270/4237/7829) would still preserve the worktree and fire escalation notifications for a story that did not escalate.
  Suggestion: When adding the outcome, enumerate every mapping table in story_state.py (_TERMINAL_OUTCOMES, _CANONICAL_TO_LEGACY_STATUS) and grep the StoryOutcome call sites in state_writer/rca/abnormal/budget_runtime/cli.sprint; branch on the decompose marker before the generic result.success handling in runner.py so no on_escalate/preserve path fires. Add a test asserting the sprint summary counts the story as returned-for-decomposition and that its worktree is not marked escalated.
- [P1-impl] [anthropic-opus-cli] Step 4 gates on state.preflight_complexity_score, the projected score. #2680 shipped in this same file (preflight_flow.py:886-892) deliberately reads scope_exceeded off implementation_score, not the projected score, because a validation-heavy story can project to 10 while its code change is one coherent unit — exactly the story a split prompt would mis-advise. Threshold 9 on the projected axis will therefore pause some stories #2680 concluded should not be split.
  Suggestion: Keep the projected score as the headline the spec's example prints, but consider anchoring the threshold comparison on preflight_implementation_complexity_score (state.py:755), or at minimum record both axes in the pending record and the audit block so the operator sees why it paused. Either choice is defensible — make it explicit in the gate module's docstring rather than implicit.
- [P2] [anthropic-opus-cli] Preflight warned that issue-2680's threshold-calibration context was not found in the repo; the plan picks 9 from COMPLEXITY_SCORE_MAX alone. #2680 is in fact shipped (preflight_flow.py:886) and treats 10 as the ceiling signal, so 9 is a reasonable default, but the plan does not record that reconciliation.
  Suggestion: Note in the config comment for the default that 9 is one below the ceiling that #2680 already flags, so the two signals do not collapse into the same story set.
- [P1-impl] [google-gemini-3.5-flash-api] Ensure the new StoryOutcome.DECOMPOSED is fully registered across status reporting and cli/watch rendering utilities so it has a clean display string 'returned for decomposition'.
